Current green: (15,37), (15,43), (51,43).
Next, the two leftmost in the upper box: (15,37) → target (15,49)?? That's outside the box. Hmm, wait: the rule is that the first green moves +12, the second moves -12. (15,37)+12 = (15,49). But (15,49) is outside the white box (the box's white ends at column 47). Hmm, but in level 1 the target was always a valid gray cell. Let me check what the border of (15,37) is.
Actually wait — maybe the rule isn't "leftmost two." Let me reconsider: in level 1, the selectable ones were (18,17) and (18,23) — the two leftmost. After the move, (18,29) and (18,35) — again the two leftmost. Then (18,41) — the only one in the column... and (24,41)? I only tested (18,41).
Here, the two leftmost are (15,37) and (15,43).
(15,37) → +12 = (15,49) — outside the box? The box's white region: columns 6-47. (15,49) is a sky-blue background. Hmm, but wait — the top box: the white bbox is (8,6,25,47). So (15,49) is outside.
Hmm, but the target might not be +12; maybe the target is the next gray cell in the direction of the other green? In level 1: (18,17) → (18,29): the other green (18,23) is to its right; target (18,29) is 6 columns to the right of (18,23). Hmm, that's "the position of the other green + 6"? (18,23)+6 = (18,29) ✓. (18,23) → (18,11): the other (18,17) is to its left; (18,17)-6 = (18,11) ✓. (18,29) → (18,41): the other (18,35) is to the right; (18,35)+6 = (18,41) ✓. (18,35) → (18,23): the other (18,29) is to the left; (18,29)-6 = (18,23) ✓. (18,41) → (30,41): the other (24,41) is below; (24,41)+6 = (30,41) ✓.
So the rule: the target = the position of the other selectable green ± 6 in the direction of the other green. Equivalently: each green's target is 6 cells beyond the other green.
So for (15,37) and (15,43): (15,37) → (15,43)+6 = (15,49). Still (15,49)! Outside the box. Hmm.
Wait, but maybe the target is clamped to the box, or maybe the target is (15,43) itself? Let me test by clicking (15,37) and reading the border.
